sentences.base_language: The party climbs the mountain toward the dragon's lair.
sentences.target_language: El grupo sube la montaña hacia la guarida del dragón.
sentences.grammarNote:
**sube** = climbs (él/ella/ellos present of **subir**, regular -ir). Here it is third-person singular with **el grupo** as subject.
**hacia** = toward — a preposition of direction; compare **hasta** (up to/as far as): **subimos hacia la cima** vs **subimos hasta la cima** (all the way to the summit).

sentences.base_language: The air smells like smoke and sulfur.
sentences.target_language: El aire huele a humo y azufre.
sentences.grammarNote:
**huele a** = smells like — **oler** (o→ue): huelo, hueles, huele, olemos, oléis, huelen. Note the **h** added before **ue** in stem-changed forms.
**azufre** (sulfur) is masculine: **el azufre** — a classic dragon-lair detail.

sentences.base_language: Suddenly, the dragon appears at the top of a cliff.
sentences.target_language: De repente, el dragón aparece en lo alto de un acantilado.
sentences.grammarNote:
**De repente** = suddenly — a narrative adverb perfect for action-packed stories.
**en lo alto de** = at the top of — **lo alto** is a nominalized adjective (lo + adjective = the [adjective] part/thing): **lo bueno** (the good thing), **lo difícil** (the hard part).

sentences.base_language: It is enormous and its scales shine like dark fire.
sentences.target_language: Es enorme y sus escamas brillan como fuego oscuro.
sentences.grammarNote:
**Es enorme** — **ser** for the dragon's inherent, permanent size — it is essentially enormous.
**brillan** = they shine (third-person plural of **brillar**, regular -ar); **escamas** (scales) is feminine plural: **las escamas**.

sentences.base_language: The dragon roars and the mountain shakes.
sentences.target_language: El dragón ruge y la montaña tiembla.
sentences.grammarNote:
**ruge** = roars (él/ella present of **rugir** — a verb with irregular yo form: **rujo** (g→j before o/a)).
**tiembla** = shakes/trembles (él/ella present of **temblar**, an e→ie stem-changing verb: tiemblo, tiemblas, tiembla, temblamos, temblais, tiemblan).

sentences.base_language: 'Don't be afraid! Attack together!' Jeffrey shouts.
sentences.grammarNote:
**¡No tengan miedo!** = Don't be afraid! — **tener miedo** (to be afraid, lit. 'to have fear'). **Tengan** is the ustedes negative imperative of **tener** (irregular).
**¡Ataquen!** is the ustedes affirmative imperative of **atacar** (c→qu before e): ataque → ataquen.

sentences.base_language: One brother casts a fireball spell at the dragon.
sentences.target_language: Un hermano lanza un hechizo de bola de fuego al dragón.
sentences.grammarNote:
**lanza** = casts/throws (él/ella present of **lanzar**, regular -ar). Preterite yo: **lancé** (z→c before e).
**bola de fuego** = fireball — literally 'ball of fire'. Spanish D&D often keeps the English term **fireball** or translates it as **esfera de fuego** (sphere of fire) depending on the edition.

sentences.base_language: The dragon is wounded but still dangerous.
sentences.target_language: El dragón está herido pero todavía es peligroso.
sentences.grammarNote:
**está herido** — **estar** for the resulting state of being wounded (a temporary condition caused by the attack).
**todavía es peligroso** — **ser** for the dragon's inherent dangerous nature — even wounded, danger is part of what it fundamentally is.

sentences.base_language: The other brother is hit by a blast of fire.
sentences.target_language: El otro hermano es golpeado por un chorro de fuego.
sentences.grammarNote:
**es golpeado por** = is hit by — passive construction: **ser + past participle + por**. The past participle **golpeado** agrees masculine with **el hermano**.
**chorro de fuego** = blast/stream of fire — **chorro** = stream/jet (of liquid, fire, etc.): **un chorro de agua** (a stream of water).

sentences.base_language: He only has eight hit points left.
sentences.target_language: Solo le quedan ocho puntos de vida.
sentences.grammarNote:
**le quedan** = he has left (lit. 'there remain to him') — **quedar** used impersonally like **gustar**: the hit points are the grammatical subject (**quedan**, plural), and **le** = to him.
**ocho** = eight — cardinal numbers are invariable in Spanish except for **uno/una** and compound numbers ending in -uno/-una.

**¡Usa!** = Use! — tú affirmative imperative of **usar** (regular -ar): drop the -s from **usas → usa**.
**¡Rápido!** = Quick!/Quickly! — used as an interjection; the adjective **rápido** functions adverbially here (Spanish often uses adjectives as adverbs in exclamations).

sentences.base_language: Jeffrey's ranger climbs a rock and aims his bow at the dragon's heart.
sentences.target_language: El explorador de Jeffrey sube a una roca y apunta su arco al corazón del dragón.
sentences.grammarNote:
**apunta** = aims (él/ella present of **apuntar**, regular -ar) — **apuntar a** = to aim at something.
**al corazón** = at the heart — **al** = mandatory contraction of **a + el**; **corazón** is masculine: **el corazón**, plural **los corazones**.

sentences.base_language: He takes a deep breath and rolls to hit.
sentences.target_language: Respira hondo y tira el dado para atacar.
sentences.grammarNote:
**Respira hondo** = takes a deep breath — literally 'breathes deep'; **hondo** (deep) is used as an adverb here (invariable).
**para atacar** = in order to attack — **para + infinitive** expresses purpose.

sentences.base_language: Natural twenty! The arrow pierces the dragon's weak spot.
sentences.target_language: ¡Veinte natural! La flecha atraviesa el punto débil del dragón.
sentences.grammarNote:
**atraviesa** = pierces/crosses (él/ella present of **atravesar**, an e→ie stem-changing verb).
**punto débil** = weak spot/weak point — **débil** (weak) is an adjective that does not change for gender (same form for masculine and feminine): **el punto débil**, **la defensa débil**.

sentences.base_language: The dragon lets out a final roar and collapses.
sentences.target_language: El dragón lanza un último rugido y se desploma.
sentences.grammarNote:
**lanza** = lets out (él/ella present of **lanzar**); **rugido** = roar (noun, masculine: **el rugido**) — from **rugir** (to roar).
**se desploma** = collapses — reflexive verb **desplomarse** (to collapse/crash down); the **se** makes the action reflexive (the dragon causes itself to fall).

sentences.base_language: The village's treasure is in the dragon's lair. The brothers have won.
sentences.target_language: El tesoro del pueblo está en la guarida del dragón. Los hermanos han ganado.
sentences.grammarNote:
**está en** — **estar** for location: the treasure is currently situated in the lair.
**han ganado** = they have won — present perfect: **haber (han)** + past participle **ganado**. Use the present perfect for events with present relevance (the victory just happened and matters now).
